Picking implementation progress, 2026-09-08

Base HEAD: 38e8c62b5b3fb74d0a32664a168e95e9f708bd49. All changes remain uncommitted.

Implemented exhaustive device-scene routing, typed/coalesced target hits, distance/cutoff/draw-order rules, rectangle and even-odd lasso selection, clipped/rotated fill and stroke geometry, point batches, nonzero polygon winding, explicit text/image bounds and transparent policy. PickViewport maps centered aspect-preserving CSS content rectangles to device pixels, including letterboxing and radius conversion without double-applying DPR.

Independent Java2D BasicStroke oracle exposed an incorrect closing join when a single dash covered an entire closed path. Chromium SVG and Canvas reproduced the expected capped seam. Fixed all dash runs to remain open; retained shared regression. All 270 BasicStroke path/cap/join/dash configurations and 108000 grid samples now pass without filtering cases or weakening the oracle.

Verification:
- sbt interactionJVM/test and interactionJS/test: 51 JVM and 49 Scala.js tests passed. Scala 3.3.8, Java 25.0.1. Log /private/tmp/intaglio-picking-tests-4.log. Earlier failing oracle log /private/tmp/intaglio-picking-tests-3.log retained.
- Production/test scalafmt completed in the same successful run; git diff --check passed.
- tools/check-picking-browser.cjs passed with Playwright 1.56.0 and Chromium 141.0.7390.37: nine SVG/Canvas stroke cases and SVG screen-coordinate fixtures at DPR 1, 1.25, 2, 3. Browser evidence /private/tmp/intaglio-picking-browser/verified.json. These are primitive fixtures, not a mounted-widget proof.
- Browser install using Node 26 stalled in archive extraction; stopped only owned installer PID 22395 and child 22396 after proving parent chain and open archive via ps/lsof, then extracted its downloaded archive with unzip. The original shared Chromium cache was incomplete and was not modified.

Still pending: full widget coordinate/lifecycle/accessibility validation, curved painted-dash capability (currently explicit Unsupported), host miter-limit alignment, full built-in target certification, spatial indexing/performance characterization, supported JDK matrix. Default continuous dash picking is explicit interaction-corridor semantics. Child 3 and epic remain open/in progress; no ggiraph baseline claim.
